sources.title: A geometric proof of the Blaschke–Lebesgue theorem for the Cheeger constant
sources.notes: Local Cheeger_BL.tex inspected; arXiv earlier title: On the Blaschke–Lebesgue theorem for the Cheeger constant via areas and perimeters of inner parallel sets. The Reuleaux triangle maximizes the Cheeger constant.

sources.notes: Local Volume_Meissner.tex inspected; arXiv:2310.17672; online 2024, journal volume 75 (2026), pp. 48–72. Convention here uses S=2π−2Σf.

sources.title: Mixed volumes and the Blaschke–Lebesgue theorem
sources.notes: Acta Mathematica Hungarica 173, 122–138 (2024), DOI 10.1007/s10474-024-01435-w. Exercises use the local 16-page preprint dated 2 May 2024; page and theorem locators refer to that version. See sources/mixed-volume-extraction.md for coverage and normalization notes.

sources.title: Unit-width bodies packed in a unit disk: problem proposed by the author
sources.notes: Problem and 120-degree-sector idea supplied in conversation on 15 October 2026. Companion exercises developed in this collection from support functions, the difference body, corner bounds and inradius bounds. No publication or novelty claim; see sources/packing-exploration.md.

sources.title: Shape Variation and Optimization: A Geometrical Analysis
sources.notes: EMS Tracts in Mathematics 28, ISBN 978-3-03719-178-1. Local English PDF inspected: Chapter 2, especially §§2.2.2–2.2.6 and selected exercises in §2.5. Printed page numbers are used. Support-function extensions are labeled separately; see sources/henrot-pierre-extraction.md.

sources.title: The Blaschke–Lebesgue theorem revisited — version 1 (two proof approaches)
sources.notes: Local 27-page preprint inspected, especially §§3–4. The variational exercises enforce closure moments explicitly and use a duality lemma; do not copy the projected perturbation admissibility claim unchecked. See sources/blaschke-proof-routes.md.

sources.title: The Blaschke–Lebesgue theorem revisited — version 2
sources.notes: Version dated 10 July 2024; §3 Lemma 3.3 inspected for the shortest-chord safeguard. This version retains the polygon proof; it does not contain the first version’s variational section. Published in Expositiones Mathematicae 42 (2024), article 125617.

sources.title: New variational arguments regarding the Blaschke–Lebesgue theorem
sources.notes: Exercises use the local BL2D_optim.tex manuscript, especially §2 finite-class existence, §3 area sensitivities and §4 center formulation. Local file fingerprint retained; numbering may differ from published editions.
